questions.question: Why must you call httpServer.listen() rather than app.listen() when using Socket.IO with Express?
options: Socket.IO is attached to the http.Server you created; app.listen() would start a separate server without Socket.IO
app.listen() does not support HTTP routes
questions.explanation: app.listen() creates a new http.Server internally. Socket.IO must share the same server instance as Express, so you create it with createServer(app) and listen on that.

questions.question: Where is the best place to authenticate a Socket.IO client?
options: In every emit call on the client
In io.use() middleware during the handshake, e.g. verifying a token from socket.handshake.auth
questions.explanation: Handshake middleware rejects unauthenticated clients before any event handler runs. Per-event authorisation is still needed for data access.

questions.question: Which call sends an event to everyone in room "order:42" except the socket that triggered it?
questions.explanation: socket.to(room).emit excludes the sender. io.to(room).emit includes everyone in the room, io.emit reaches all clients, and socket.emit replies only to that one client.

questions.question: You scale a Socket.IO app to three instances and room broadcasts only reach some users. What is missing?
options: An adapter such as the Redis adapter so instances share broadcasts (plus sticky sessions if long polling is used)
questions.explanation: Each instance only knows its own sockets. An adapter relays broadcasts between instances, and sticky sessions keep long-polling requests on one instance.
